cards.d: To adapt means to change in order to deal with a new situation or addition.
cards.e: When he went to the new town, he had to adapt to all the weather changes.

cards.d: Biological describes the process of life and living things.
cards.e: In science, we learned about the biological process of bacterial growth.

cards.d: When something is cellular, it relates to the cells of animals or plants.
cards.e: She used a microscope to see the activity at a cellular level.

cards.d: When people are dynamic, they are lively and have creative ideas.
cards.e: The new, dynamic employee came up with a good way to juggle his work load.

cards.d: A fantasy is a pleasant situation that people think about but is unlikely to happen.
cards.e: Becoming an astronaut is a fantasy shared by many children.

cards.d: Heredity is the process of passing on features from parents to children.
cards.e: The boy’s face is similar to his father’s because of heredity.

cards.d: When something is internal, it exists or happens inside a person, object, or place.
cards.e: We removed the outer case to reveal the computer’s internal wires.

cards.d: When something is minimal, it is very small.
cards.e: My lazy husband does a minimal amount of work around the house.

cards.d: A pioneer is a person who is the first to discover or be involved in something.
cards.e: He was a pioneer of computer programming.

cards.d: To prescribe medicine means to tell someone to take it.
cards.e: When I was sick, the doctor prescribed me flu medicine.

cards.d: When things are respective, they relate separately to each person just mentioned.
cards.e: The boxers were told to return to their respective corners.

cards.d: To revive someone or something means to restore health or life to them.
cards.e: She revived the feeling of warmth in her leg by rubbing it softly.

cards.d: When rules or systems are rigid, they are severe because they cannot be changed.
cards.e: Societies often have rigid rules about the way that people are supposed to act.

cards.d: A sequence is a number of events or things that come one after another.
cards.e: The dominos fell in a sequence of one after another.

cards.d: To substitute something or someone means to have them take the place of another.
cards.e: When I ran out of juice, I had to substitute water to drink in the morning.

cards.d: A surgeon is a doctor who is trained to do surgery.
cards.e: The surgeon operated on the old man’s heart.

cards.d: Therapy is treatment for a particular physical or mental illness or condition.
cards.e: After she broke her legs, she used physical therapy to learn how to walk again.

cards.d: To transfer something means to move it from one place to another.
cards.e: The family transferred the groceries from the shopping cart to the car.

cards.d: A transition is a process where there is a change from one form to another.
cards.e: The weather gets colder during the transition from summer to autumn.

cards.d: A transplant is an operation in which a damaged part of one’s body is replaced.
cards.e: The sick child needed a heart transplant to live.
